# AI that acts<br> in the studio,<br> on stage,<br> in the world.

<p class="lede">We build AI that works inside the instruments, tools and spaces artists already use: DAWs and plug-ins, collections and archives, installations and stages. Not a chatbot beside them, but agents that see the whole environment, act in it safely, and notice what changed. So far: Sideman for Ableton Live, Kiln for creative coding, Dandelion for learning to code.</p>

<p class="audience">For music-tech companies, labels and studios, museums and galleries, festivals and artists.</p>

::: {.layers}
::: {.layer .perceive}
<div class="eyebrow c-perceive">Layer one</div>
### Perceive
What the model can see decides what it can do. We build the senses: bridges into an application's object model, observers that report what a human did by hand, embeddings over a collection, sensors on a stage.
:::
::: {.layer .reason}
<div class="eyebrow c-reason">Layer two</div>
### Reason
Grammars, skills and evaluation. We teach the model how a domain is shaped so it looks instead of guessing, and we measure coverage against the real system rather than claiming it.
:::
::: {.layer .act}
<div class="eyebrow c-act">Layer three</div>
### Act
Real writes with real undo, sound, light and machines that answer in real time, and a guard before anything destructive. An agent that acts has to be safe to be wrong.
:::
:::

## Why Sisyphe

::: {.measure}
Sisyphus pushed the same rock up the same hill, forever. Creative work has more of that than anyone admits: the fortieth track rename, the stems you export one more time, the catalogue you re-tag by hand, the cue you rebuild because one setting was wrong. It all has to be done, and none of it needs you.

We build the thing that pushes the rock. You keep the part that needs you: the taste, the judgment, the call.
:::
